title: Window opening steps return WindowProxy despite COOP

labels.name: topic: cross-origin-opener-policy
labels.description: Issues and ideas around the new "inverse of rel=noopener" header

body:
Currently, the cross-origin opener policy influences [the rules for choosing a browsing context](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#the-rules-for-choosing-a-browsing-context-given-a-browsing-context-name):

> [...]
> 1. If current's top-level browsing context's active document's cross-origin opener policy is "same-origin" or "same-origin-plus-COEP", then:
>    1. Let currentDocument be current's active document.
>    2. If currentDocument's origin is not same origin with currentDocument's relevant settings object's top-level origin, then set noopener to true and name to "_blank".
> 2. Set new to true.
> 3. If noopener is true, then set chosen to the result of creating a new top-level browsing context.
> 4. Otherwise:
>    1. Set chosen to the result of creating a new auxiliary browsing context with current.
>    2. If sandboxingFlagSet's sandboxed navigation browsing context flag is set, then current must be set as chosen's one permitted sandboxed navigator.
>    [...]

COOP influences the value of the variable name "noopener", and this in turn alters the observable behavior of the algorithm.

However, when this algorithm is called from [the window open steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#window-open-steps), the related (but independent) variable named "noopener" has a further effect:

> [...]
> 9. Let target browsing context and new be the result of applying the rules for choosing a browsing context given target, source browsing context, and noopener.
> 10. If target browsing context is null, then return null.
> [...]
> 14. If noopener is true, then return null.
> 15. Otherwise, if new is false, set target browsing context's opener browsing context to source browsing context.
> 16. Return target browsing context's WindowProxy object.

I believe the intent is that COOP enforcement should cause `window.open` and `document.open` to return `null`. The latest builds of Firefox and Chrome both behave this way. However, the algorithm appears to specify that the WindowProxy should be returned because:

- the "rules for choosing a browsing context" algorithm returns a browsing context (so the branch in step 10 above is not taken)
- "noopener" is not influenced by COOP because "primitive" parameters like the boolean "noopener" are not passed "by reference" (so the branch in step 14 is not taken)

Is this interpretation correct?
